lesson.title: Late Is the Culprit
lesson.hook: Your forehand keeps flying wide, so you change everything except when you hit it.
lesson.memHTML: The miss tells you when you hit it.
lesson.tomorrow: Next time your forehand sprays the same way twice, check your contact: was the ball out in front, or beside your hip?

drill.name: Turn on "bounce"
drill.how: Rally crosscourt and say "bounce" as the ball bounces on your side. Your shoulders must already be turned by the word. Count the forehands that leave straight, not wide.

lesson.cue: Turn early. Meet it in front.

steps.name: Wide to the right
steps.sit: You aim crosscourt, but your forehand flies wide to the right. Watch it again, held at contact.
steps.q: What do you change on the next ball?
opts: Hit it higher over the net
steps.payoff: The ball was beside your hip. Out in front, it went where you aimed.
steps.principle: A forehand that sprays right was hit late.
steps.why: Met late, the racquet face still points to the right, and the ball follows the face. Pace, height and spin don't turn the face; meeting it earlier does.
steps.take: Forehand flying wide right? Meet it out in front.

lines.A: Still late — harder, and it flies wide again.
lines.B: Still late — higher, but the face still sends it wide.
lines.C: Out in front, the face points crosscourt — deep, rally on.
lines.D: Still late — more spin, same direction: wide.

steps.name: A faster ball
steps.sit: A bigger, faster ball comes to your forehand. Late again, and wide again.
steps.q: What gets you there in time?
opts: A bigger take-back for more power
steps.payoff: Starting early put the contact back out in front.
steps.principle: You fix late at the start of the swing, not the end.
steps.why: Against pace, the swing has less time. Turning early with a shorter take-back gets the racquet there on time; a bigger take-back or a later start makes you later still.
steps.take: Late against pace? Turn early, take it back shorter.

lines.A: Bigger take-back, even later — it flies further wide.
lines.B: A later start, even later contact — wider still.
lines.C: Faster, but still late — wide again.
lines.D: Early turn, contact in front — deep, rally on.

steps.name: Backhand, pulled to the middle
steps.sit: Now your backhand won't go crosscourt: it keeps pulling left, into the middle. Held at contact again.
steps.q: What do you change on the next ball?
opts: Hit it higher over the net
steps.payoff: Same culprit on the other wing: late, so the face pointed left, off your line.
steps.principle: Where the ball pulls to tells you it was late.
steps.why: A late backhand pulls left, just as a late forehand pushes right. Either way the ball goes where the face points, so meet it earlier.
steps.take: Backhand pulling into the middle? Late again: meet it in front.

lines.A: Out in front, the face points crosscourt — deep, rally on.
lines.B: Still late — higher, but it still pulls to the middle.
lines.C: Still late — harder, and it pulls to the middle again.
lines.D: Still late — more spin, same direction: the middle.
